audience: a parent or patient-group leader without medical training

sentences.text: Krabbe disease is linked to the gene GALC in curated databases, with no contradicting evidence [e_3dbc42738b5a].
Metachromatic leukodystrophy is linked to the gene ARSA, but this link is text_mined, which means it was extracted from literature and is unverified [e_deb97136f1d7].

Both diseases are also linked to a third gene, PSAP, but only by inference from subtypes, with confidence 0.475 for Krabbe disease and 0.45 for metachromatic leukodystrophy [e_2c5236d2f740] [e_eafba62e86fa].
Those PSAP links hold for the named subtypes and not necessarily for every form of each disease [e_2c5236d2f740] [e_eafba62e86fa].
GALC, ARSA and PSAP all take part in the same curated pathway, glycosphingolipid catabolism [e_993c3f6ead03] [e_6331a370f2a1] [e_8f8f3574e614].
The two diseases look somewhat alike in their listed symptoms, but this is only a computed score (simGIC 0.216) from Constellate [e_e270315fe572].
For Krabbe disease, one trial is listed as not yet recruiting and one as terminated, which is a record of studies and not a sign that anything works [e_b85030c9d696] [e_75f4a2222b59].
These edges do not show how the diseases differ in daily life, since the symptom edges are for metachromatic leukodystrophy and one is text_mined [e_1e9c9c4e3bd1] [e_d896e966c8de].
